title: GitOps, CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code
description: Continuous Integration, automated test pipelines, declarative IaC with Terraform, and GitOps deployments.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Continuous Integration (CI)?
options: Automatically build and run automated tests on code changes whenever developers commit
Deploy code directly to production without staging or reviews
Shut down unused development servers at midnight
Replace all unit testing with manual QA verification

questions.question: What paradigm manages infrastructure configuration declaratively through version-controlled files?
options: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
Manual Server Provisioning
Direct SSH Administration
Ad-hoc Terminal Scripting

questions.question: In GitOps (e.g. ArgoCD or Flux), what acts as the single source of truth for desired system state?
options: A Git repository containing declarative manifests
The live in-memory etcd cluster
A developer's local docker-compose file
The Slack deployment channel notification history

questions.question: Which deployment strategy keeps old and new versions active and switches traffic instantly at the router level?
options: Blue-Green Deployment
In-place Mutation
Rolling Single-Instance Restart
Shadow Cold-Start

questions.question: Why is signed provenance (e.g., Sigstore / Cosign) crucial in build pipelines?
options: It cryptographically proves that a container image was built by the authorized CI workflow from exact source commits
It speeds up npm install execution by 40%
It converts x86 binaries into ARM64 instructions
It bypasses Kubernetes admission controllers automatically
